source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

chapter_binding.source_omission_reason: Absent from pinned SBLGNT; the parent Fluent already preserves this numbering gap.
chapter_binding.tsw_omission_reason: TSW also lacks these public labels; comparator bytes unchanged.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the title and Jesus’ indirect reply without turning it into a simple yes or no.
key_decisions.before: Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “You say so.”
key_decisions.after: Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered him, “You say so.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” And answering him, he said, “You say so.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves Barabbas’s name, companions, rebellion, and actual killing.
key_decisions.before: A man called Barabbas was in prison with rebels who had committed murder during an uprising.
key_decisions.after: A man called Barabbas was imprisoned with rebels who had committed murder during the uprising.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And there was one called Barabbas, bound with the rebels who had committed murder in the uprising.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps Pilate’s motive, release, ordered violence, and handing over for execution.
key_decisions.before: Wanting to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. After having Jesus flogged, he handed him over to be crucified.
key_decisions.after: Wanting to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas for them. He had Jesus flogged and handed him over to be crucified.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them, and having flogged Jesus, handed him over to be crucified.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves Mark’s explanation of the location and the full military unit.
key_decisions.before: The soldiers led Jesus inside the courtyard—that is, the governor’s headquarters—and called together the whole cohort.
key_decisions.after: The soldiers led Jesus inside the courtyard—that is, the governor’s headquarters—and called together the whole cohort.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And the soldiers led him away inside the courtyard, that is, the governor’s headquarters, and they called together the whole cohort.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the repeated assault, spitting, kneeling, and ironic act without calling it sincere worship.
key_decisions.before: They struck his head with a reed, spit on him, and knelt down in mock homage.
key_decisions.after: They kept striking his head with a reed and spitting on him. They knelt down and paid him mocking homage.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And they were striking his head with a reed and spitting on him, and kneeling down they were paying homage to him.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves coercion, Simon’s origin and movement, his sons’ names, and the cross.
key_decisions.before: They compelled a passerby, Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country—the father of Alexander and Rufus—to carry Jesus’ cross.
key_decisions.after: They forced a passerby to carry Jesus’ cross: Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the countryside, the father of Alexander and Rufus.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And they compelled a passerby, Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the exact mixture and Jesus’ refusal without assigning a motive.
key_decisions.before: They offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.
key_decisions.after: They offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And they were giving him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains Mark’s ancient time notation and the repeated execution statement.
key_decisions.before: It was the third hour when they crucified him.
key_decisions.after: It was the third hour when they crucified him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And it was the third hour when they crucified him.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps two violent criminals and their positions without importing conversation from another Gospel.
key_decisions.before: They crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and one on his left.
key_decisions.after: They crucified two bandits with him, one on his right and one on his left.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And with him they crucified two robbers, one on his right and one on his left.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves reviling, gesture, taunt, and the unfinished accusation flowing to verse 30.
key_decisions.before: Those passing by reviled him, shaking their heads and saying, “Ha! You who would destroy the temple and build it in three days,
key_decisions.after: Those passing by reviled him, shaking their heads and saying, “Ha! You who would tear down the temple and build it in three days,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And those passing by were blaspheming him, shaking their heads and saying, “Ha! The one who destroys the temple and builds it in three days,

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps both titles, demanded sign, stated belief condition, and the co-crucified men’s abuse.
key_decisions.before: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down from the cross now, so that we may see and believe.” Those crucified with him also insulted him.
key_decisions.after: Let the Messiah, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe.” Those crucified with him also insulted him.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe.” And those crucified with him were reproaching him.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains both ancient times, darkness, and its full spatial scope without choosing land or earth cosmology beyond context.
key_decisions.before: When the sixth hour came, darkness covered the whole land until the ninth hour.
key_decisions.after: When the sixth hour came, darkness covered the whole land until the ninth hour.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And when the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the Aramaic cry, Mark’s translation, repeated address, and raw abandonment.
key_decisions.before: At the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
key_decisions.after: At the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which is translated, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the bystanders’ interpretation as their own speech and the attention command.
key_decisions.before: When some standing nearby heard this, they said, “Look, he is calling Elijah.”
key_decisions.after: When some of those standing nearby heard it, they said, “Listen, he is calling Elijah.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And some of those standing by, hearing it, said, “Behold, he is calling Elijah.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the unnamed person, each action, sour wine, and Elijah test without adding compassion or hostility.
key_decisions.before: Someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink, saying, “Wait. Let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
key_decisions.after: Someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave it to Jesus to drink, saying, “Wait! Let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave him drink, saying, “Leave him; let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the final cry and death in the source’s restrained language.
key_decisions.before: But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed his last.
key_decisions.after: Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed his last.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But Jesus, uttering a loud cry, breathed his last.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the full direction and extent of the tearing without supplying an agent or interpretation.
key_decisions.before: The curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
key_decisions.after: The curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And the curtain of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the centurion’s location, the manner of death as occasion, and the confession without an added article claim.
key_decisions.before: When the centurion standing opposite Jesus saw that he breathed his last in this way, he said, “Truly this man was God’s Son.”
key_decisions.after: When the centurion standing opposite Jesus saw that he breathed his last in this way, he said, “Truly this man was God’s Son.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And when the centurion, who stood opposite him, saw that in this way he breathed his last, he said, “Truly this man was God’s Son.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves distance, all three women, both sons’ names, and James’s descriptor.
key_decisions.before: Some women were also watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and Joses, and Salome.
key_decisions.after: Some women were also watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and Joses, and Salome.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Now there were also women watching from a distance, among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome,

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps women as followers and servants, Galilee, and the larger group’s journey to Jerusalem.
key_decisions.before: When Jesus was in Galilee, these women had followed him and served him. Many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem were also there.
key_decisions.after: When Jesus was in Galilee, these women followed him and served him. Many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem were also there.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: who, when he was in Galilee, followed him and served him, and many other women who came up with him to Jerusalem.

key_decisions.rationale: Retains the late time and Mark’s explanation of the named day while continuing the sentence.
key_decisions.before: Evening had already come. Since it was Preparation Day, the day before the Sabbath,
key_decisions.after: Evening had already come. Since it was Preparation Day—that is, the day before the Sabbath—
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And when evening had already come, since it was Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath,

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps Joseph’s origin, status, kingdom hope, courage, and request for the body.
key_decisions.before: Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member who was himself waiting for the kingdom of God, came and boldly went to Pilate to ask for Jesus’ body.
key_decisions.after: Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member who was himself waiting for God’s kingdom, came and boldly went in to Pilate to ask for Jesus’ body.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Joseph of Arimathea came, a respected council member, who also himself was waiting for the kingdom of God. Taking courage, he went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves Pilate’s surprise, reliance on the centurion, and question about elapsed time.
key_decisions.before: Pilate was surprised that Jesus was already dead. He summoned the centurion and asked whether Jesus had been dead for some time.
key_decisions.after: Pilate was surprised that Jesus was already dead. He summoned the centurion and asked whether he had been dead for some time.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Pilate was amazed that he had already died. And summoning the centurion, he asked him whether he had been dead for some time.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the verification, Pilate’s grant, and the source’s stark corpse term.
key_decisions.before: After learning from the centurion that Jesus was dead, Pilate gave the body to Joseph.
key_decisions.after: After learning from the centurion that Jesus was dead, Pilate granted the corpse to Joseph.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And learning from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps both named witnesses and their observation linking burial to the next scene.
key_decisions.before: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching where he was laid.
key_decisions.after: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching where Jesus was laid.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching where he was laid.
